scope: Static inspection of already downloaded character/weapon modeling tools, native examples and related original fixtures; no network, executables, installations or corpus changes.

coverage.not_entire_download_archive: Root agent owns full native-asset inventory; this report is a selected tool lane.

sources.author: SavageX
sources.evidence: Original retained ZIP bytes independently opened, member inventory and hashes measured; no binaries run.
sources.limitations: Native template only; bundled Word document not decoded, HTML inventoried not used as new source. No rights to redistribute stock-derived hand geometry inferred.
sources.finding: Native 3DO 2.1 contains 16 material slots, with slots 0–8 dflt placeholders and 9–15 hand/arm materials. Four meshes and five nodes include an empty K_WEAPON mesh attached below the hand. Preserve explicit mesh references and remap material indices; nine slots is a template layout, not an engine limit.

sources.author: Frank Krueger (program catalog attribution)
sources.evidence: Original retained ZIP bytes independently opened, member inventory and hashes measured; no binaries run.
sources.limitations: Single executable only; no source, manual, example, observed CLI or conversion result. Catalog describes ASC to 3DO.
sources.finding: Catalog credits Frank Krueger with ASC-to-3DO conversion, but retained package contains only one executable. No documented unattended interface or observed output was established.

sources.author: Code Alliance
sources.evidence: Original retained ZIP bytes independently opened, member inventory and hashes measured; no binaries run.
sources.limitations: Two members only. WinHelp present and hashed, not decoded. 0.7 tutorial features cannot be assigned to 0.61. No runtime/source/CLI verification.
sources.finding: The usable 0.61 ZIP has an executable and WinHelp file only. WinHelp was not decoded. The separate PJB tutorial discusses 0.7, so its UI claims cannot be assigned to this binary.

sources.author: Jereth Kok
sources.evidence: Original retained ZIP bytes independently opened, member inventory and hashes measured; no binaries run.
sources.limitations: Trajectory example is a vehicle, not a humanoid rig. Demo author warns of vertical-flight flip. Level layout excluded. No runtime or animation-retarget proof.
sources.finding: Jereth Kok supplies a one-node trajectory KEY with 171 frames at 8 FPS and 171 entry rows. His manual reports a vertical-flight flip; rotation wrap and loop transitions are useful original test cases. This is not a character-retargeting demonstration.

sources.author: Curtis Brazzell (program catalog attribution)
sources.evidence: Original retained ZIP bytes independently opened, member inventory and hashes measured; no binaries run.
sources.limitations: Installer not opened or run. Readme makes historical OS/default-path assumptions and anticipates Patch Commander integration in a later release. No MotS or modern Windows compatibility established.
sources.finding: Readme describes BMP-based character editing and client-side resource agreement for multiplayer. Treat path, component and packaging instructions as historical; installer was not run and later Patch Commander integration is only anticipated.

sources.author: Zymotico
sources.evidence: Original retained ZIP bytes independently opened, member inventory and hashes measured; no binaries run.
sources.limitations: Viewer manual states first-transparent-mesh rendering issue. OpenGL lighting/environment mapping differs from engine. No runtime/CLI claim.
sources.finding: Manual documents alternate display/shading modes and a transparent-first-mesh issue. The native example has two meshes, three nodes and labels that differ between mesh definitions and hierarchy references; numeric references govern association.
